conflicts.meeting_title: DPS Board of Education -District 3 Candidate Selection
conflicts.issue: Selection of District 3 Board Vacancy Appointee (Jessica Carda-Auten vs. Kevin Primus)
conflicts.summary: The six seated board members split 4-2 in selecting a District 3 appointee to serve through June 30, 2024, dividing between public health researcher and PTA parent Jessica Carda-Auten and community advocate/researcher Kevin Primus.
conflicts.side_a_position: Appoint Jessica Carda-Auten based on her public health expertise, DPS parent and PTA involvement, collaborative demeanor, and readiness for Growing Together.
side_a_arguments: Carda-Auten brings public health and data-driven expertise, strong relationships with educators, principals, and county commissioners, and deep investment as a DPS parent.
Her collaborative listening style across differences equips the board to navigate tough Growing Together redistricting conversations and eliminate the school-to-prison pipeline.
conflicts.side_b_position: Appoint Kevin Primus for his urgency on youth violence, focus on trauma-informed/EC/ELL metrics, and broad community coalition support.
side_b_arguments: Primus demonstrated data-driven focus on EC, ELL, and trauma-informed training alongside broad research connections (Mayo Clinic, Duke, UC Davis) and community accountability amid ongoing youth gun violence.
Community leaders and coalition signatories rallied strongly behind his candidacy.
conflicts.resolution: Kevin Primus's nomination failed 2-4 and Jessica Carda-Auten's nomination passed 4-2 on roll call votes.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 2/9/23
conflicts.issue: Election of Board Vice Chair and Board Communication/Leadership Process
conflicts.summary: Following Matt Sears's resignation, the board split 3-3 across two rounds between nominees Emily Chávez and Jovonia Lewis amid pointed debate over rotational leadership, prior experience, and alleged cliques/exclusionary communication before Chair Bettina Umstead broke the tie for Chávez on the third ballot.
conflicts.side_a_position: Elect Emily Chávez as Vice Chair to bring new energy, rotational leadership, and collaborative focus
side_a_arguments: Chávez brought budget advisory co-chair experience, an intersectional equity lens, and strong relationships with commissioners and colleagues.
Supporting Chávez aligned with rotational leadership and moving the board's agenda forward after two deadlocked ballots.
conflicts.side_b_position: Elect Jovonia Lewis based on three years of board experience and push back against perceived pre-arranged cliques and exclusionary communication
side_b_arguments: Lewis argued that after three years on the board—including pandemic leadership and prior service—experience and transparency should outweigh experimentation, noting Beyer had previously said she lacked experience in her first year.
Valladares criticized perceived pre-arranged whip counts, side meetings with partners like the DPS Foundation and Self-Help, and inequitable communication excluding certain board members.
conflicts.resolution: After Round 1 (Chávez) and Round 2 (Lewis) both tied 3-3, Bettina Umstead switched from voting against both nominees to voting Aye for Emily Chávez in Round 3, electing Chávez 4-2; Valladares requested Policy Committee review of Policy 220 officer terms.

conflicts.meeting_title: DPS Board of Education -District 3 Candidate Selection
conflicts.issue: Nomination of Kevin Primus for District 3 Board Seat
conflicts.summary: Following a coin toss setting Kevin Primus first on the ballot, Alexandra Valladares nominated Primus and voted Aye alongside Jovonia Lewis, while Millicent Rogers, Natalie Beyer, Emily Chávez, and Chair Bettina Umstead voted No, failing 2-4.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 2/9/23
conflicts.issue: Board Member Resignations for DPS Foundation Roles and Conflict-of-Interest Guidelines
conflicts.summary: Following public criticism of Matt Sears resigning to join the DPS Foundation shortly after another former member did the same, board members differed on whether to pursue MOU/policy guardrails on board-to-foundation transitions versus defending former members' ethics.
conflicts.side_a_position: Explore MOU or board policy guidelines (such as recusal during interviews or a cooling-off period) to prevent the appearance of conflicts of interest
side_a_arguments: The public raised concerns about two board members stepping down to work at the DPS Foundation while participating in budget and housing discussions involving the foundation.
Clearer notice or cooling-off rules in an MOU could protect public trust without implying wrongdoing.
conflicts.side_b_position: Defend the ethical record of former members and avoid implying misconduct or adopting overly broad restrictions
side_b_arguments: Board counsel (Tharrington Smith) confirmed no legal conflict existed and both former members stepped down voluntarily to avoid even the appearance of conflict.
Legal counsel cautioned against foundation-specific rules that could hinder employment or complicate partnerships with aligned nonprofits.
conflicts.resolution: No formal motion was taken on an MOU change; later in the meeting, Lewis's request to separate the $1 million teacher-housing reserve from the DPS Foundation in the MacKenzie Scott grant motion was adopted unanimously.

meetings.title: DPS Board of Education -District 3 Candidate Selection
meetings.executive_summary: In a specially called 39-minute meeting with Alexandra Valladares joining remotely via Zoom, the six seated members of the Board of Education met to appoint a replacement for the vacant District 3 seat through June 30, 2024. After unanimously approving the agenda, board members debated the qualifications and alignment of four applicants, dividing between Kevin Primus and Jessica Carda-Auten. Valladares and Jovonia Lewis backed Primus for his data-driven focus on EC/ELL and trauma-informed metrics, extensive research network, and community coalition backing, while Natalie Beyer, Millicent Rogers, Emily Chávez, and Chair Bettina Umstead favored Carda-Auten for her public health expertise, PTA and DPS parent engagement, relationships with local officials, and collaborative approach to Growing Together. Following a coin flip to set the voting order, the board rejected Primus's nomination 2-4 and voted 4-2 to appoint Jessica Carda-Auten to the District 3 seat.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead called the special meeting to order with Alexandra Valladares participating via Zoom and led a moment of silence. On roll call, all six seated members voted unanimously (6-0) to approve the agenda.

agenda_items.title: District 3 Vacancy Deliberation and Candidate Selection
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members delivered comments weighing the four District 3 applicants before holding formal nominations determined by a coin toss (won by Kevin Primus's side to go first). On roll call votes, Alexandra Valladares's nomination of Kevin Primus failed 2-4 (Valladares and Jovonia Lewis voting Aye), and Bettina Umstead's nomination of Jessica Carda-Auten passed 4-2 (Millicent Rogers, Natalie Beyer, Emily Chávez, and Umstead voting Aye).

votes.item_title: Approval of March 16, 2023 Special Meeting Agenda
votes.notes: District 3 seat vacant; Alexandra Valladares participated via Zoom. Mover and seconder names not stated aloud.
votes.discussion_detail: The agenda as presented was moved and seconded, and all six seated board members voted Aye by roll call.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 3/9/23
meetings.executive_summary: At its March 9, 2023 work session, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education unanimously adopted a resolution opposing North Carolina House Bill 187 (Equality in Education), approved a negotiated contract for a new financial and human resources ERP system, and proclaimed March 2023 as Arts in Our Schools Month. The board received an update on upcoming two-part LGBTQIA+ governance trainings scheduled for April 21 and May 19, 2023, along with Strategic Plan Priority 4 (family and community engagement) and Priority 5 (fiscal and operational responsibility, including transportation and disparity study needs) updates. The board also unanimously approved a $1,500 ESSER-funded retention bonus (about $7.5 million total) to be paid in September 2023 to returning employees, and approved the March 9, 2023 personnel report following closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, Agenda Approval, and Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead called the work session to order, recognized the Spanish interpreters, and led a moment of silence. The board approved the evening's agenda and the February 9, 2023 work session minutes, with one board member (Jovonia Lewis) noted as arriving later due to a prior commitment.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment and Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Two speakers addressed the board during public comment: Minister Paul Scott urged the board to adopt the resolution opposing House Bill 187 ahead of its legislative committee hearing, and Kevin Primus expressed support for the Arts in Our Schools Month proclamation and urged integration of arts across core subjects while commenting on a recent community incident. Following public comment, the board approved the consent agenda without discussion.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Opposing North Carolina House Bill 187
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members read aloud in full a resolution opposing House Bill 187 ('Equality in Education'), arguing the bill would restrict educators from teaching accurate U.S. and North Carolina history regarding slavery, Jim Crow, women's suffrage, and systemic racism, and reaffirming DPS's equity commitments and legislative priorities. Board members noted minor grammatical edits to be cleaned up with the board clerk without altering content.

agenda_items.title: Contract for New Financial and Human Resources (ERP) System
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Staff Tanya Giovanni presented the finalized legal terms of the contract for DPS's new financial and human resources ERP system following negotiations with board attorneys and staff. She noted that no substantive or financial terms had changed since CFO Paul LeSieur's February 9 presentation and requested formal board approval of the finalized contract.

agenda_items.title: Update on LGBTQIA+ Board and Cabinet Training
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Staff Tanya Giovanni and Vice Chair Emily Chávez presented logistical plans for two governance trainings (101 on April 21, 2023 and 201 on May 19, 2023) at the Minnie Forte-Brown Staff Development Center, costing roughly $5,600 for speakers including NSBA legal counsel and Gender Spectrum. Board members discussed whether to invite the LGBTQIA+ task force once finalized and agreed to livestream the educational lecture portions with Spanish interpretation while keeping interactive board/cabinet workshop segments unstreamed.

agenda_items.title: Arts in Our Schools Month Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Director of Arts Education Jeremy Tucker highlighted district arts programming, including the Evening to Shine showcase at DPAC with over 500 student performers and first-time Spanish streaming and ASL interpretation, and previewed spring arts events. Board members read aloud and adopted the proclamation designating March 1-31, 2023 as Arts in Our Schools Month.

agenda_items.title: Strategic Plan Priority 4 Update: School, Family, and Community Engagement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Schools Dr. Stacey Stewart, Chief Communications Officer William Sudderth, Dr. Dietrich Tanner, and Sheena Cooper presented Priority 4 updates on family engagement, Teacher Working Conditions survey trends (noting 2022 declines), parent ambassadors, and community partnerships at every school. Board members—including Jovonia Lewis, who arrived during the discussion—pressed for a partnership evaluation rubric, expanded Multilingual Resource Center (MRC) capacity, college access partnerships, and school-level communications toolkits for Growing Together.

agenda_items.title: ESSER-Funded $1,500 Employee Retention Bonus for September 2023
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Paul LeSieur proposed a $1,500 retention bonus (pro-rated with a $500 floor) funded from expiring PRC 171 and PRC 181 ESSER federal relief dollars at an estimated total cost of $7.5 million, payable in September 2023 to all employees in payroll status as of August 31, 2023. Board members welcomed the bonus while questioning how DPS will sustain educator compensation and operational positions once federal ESSER funds expire in 2024.

agenda_items.title: Strategic Plan Priority 5 Update: Fiscal and Operational Responsibility
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy Superintendent Dr. Julius Monk and operations leaders presented Priority 5 updates covering quarterly ESSER reporting, bus transportation efficiency, driver recruitment and working conditions, and capital maintenance. Board members raised questions about post-ESSER operating funding needs (estimated near $15 million annually), middle school track resurfacing, and identifying approximately $300,000 internally to fund a DPS disparity study after partner jurisdictions could not collaborate.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted to enter closed session at 02:55:48 and reconvened in open session at 03:52:24, where Superintendent Pascal Mubenga requested approval of the March 9, 2023 personnel report. The board approved the personnel report unanimously and adjourned.

votes.notes: Jovonia Lewis arrived later in the meeting.
votes.discussion_detail: Routine approval of the March 9, 2023 work session agenda as presented.

votes.notes: Jovonia Lewis arrived later in the meeting.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the minutes from the February 9, 2023 work session.

votes.notes: Chair Bettina Umstead noted one board member (Jovonia Lewis) was absent due to a prior commitment and would arrive later.
votes.discussion_detail: Board members read the resolution opposing House Bill 187 aloud and approved it with minor non-substantive grammatical edits.

votes.notes: Jovonia Lewis arrived later in the meeting.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the finalized contract terms for the new financial and human resources ERP system following legal review.

votes.notes: Jovonia Lewis arrived later during Priority 4 presentation.
votes.discussion_detail: Proclaimed March 1-31, 2023 as Arts in Our Schools Month across Durham Public Schools.

votes.notes: All six seated board members were present.
votes.discussion_detail: Authorized a $1,500 ESSER-funded retention bonus (pro-rated, $500 minimum floor, ~$7.5 million total) to be paid in September 2023 to all staff in payroll status as of August 31, 2023.

votes.discussion_detail: Board entered closed session for reasons stated on the agenda.

meetings.title: DPS Board of Education -District 3 Candidate Interviews
meetings.executive_summary: On March 8, 2023, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education held public candidate interviews to fill the vacant District 3 seat created by former Vice Chair Matt Sears's resignation. Four eligible District 3 applicants—Jessica Carter-Oton, April Lawson Day, Kevin Primus, and Jessica Freelander—delivered timed 10-minute presentations addressing four standard board prompts on superintendent evaluation metrics, equity, engaging marginalized communities, and school safety, followed by two-minute responses on one self-selected and one randomly drawn policy topic. Vice Chair Emily Chávez participated virtually while the remaining five board members attended in person; no board deliberations or votes occurred, with the appointment vote scheduled for a special called meeting on March 16, 2023.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Interview Format Overview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead opened the meeting, recognized Vice Chair Emily Chávez attending virtually, and read aloud the four standardized interview prompts and the list of policy topics for the two-minute impromptu segments. She noted that board members would listen without asking live follow-up questions during the presentations.

agenda_items.title: District 3 Candidate Interview: Jessica Carter-Oton
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jessica Carter-Oton, a UNC qualitative public health researcher and Lakewood Elementary parent, emphasized closing the opportunity gap with disaggregated data, recruiting Black and Latinx educators, expanding enrollment, and addressing magnet-versus-base resource inequities through Growing Together. She advocated data-driven, non-fear-based school safety measures, restorative justice fidelity, and full implementation of the classified staff salary study.

agenda_items.title: District 3 Candidate Interview: April Lawson Day
agenda_items.discussion_summary: April Lawson Day, a DPS parent with legal and government experience, highlighted disproportionate discipline for students of color and students with disabilities, advocated proactive mental health screenings, and proposed evaluating the superintendent on strategic, cultural, and managerial leadership. In her two-minute topics, she called for competitive compensation including for substitutes and part-time staff and balanced budgets across secondary Growing Together boundary planning.

agenda_items.title: District 3 Candidate Interview: Kevin Primus
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Kevin Primus, a father of five DPS students, former Wake County teacher, and Riverside High School Improvement Team member, proposed evaluating the superintendent on Growing Together community engagement, educator recruitment, and trauma-informed training to close the 'engagement gap.' He stressed stronger feeder-school academic alignment between middle and high schools and expanding pipelines with Durham Tech and NCCU for bilingual, EC, and educators of color.

agenda_items.title: District 3 Candidate Interview: Jessica Freelander
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a brief recess, Jessica Freelander, a nine-year former teacher and advanced academic coordinator at Riverside High School, focused on disproportionate suspension rates, charter school impacts, dual-identified EC/ESL service gaps, and expanding honors/advanced course access for historically marginalized students. She emphasized mental health and social-emotional safety as well as job satisfaction and financial support for educator recruitment and retention.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 2/23/23
meetings.executive_summary: At its February 23, 2023 monthly meeting (with Board Member Jovonia Lewis absent on medical leave), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education recognized students and staff of the month, promoted CROWN Act Week celebrations, and heard public comments on House Bill 187 and school athletic track conditions. The board finalized the District 3 vacancy interview questions and schedule (March 7-8 interviews and a March 16 appointment vote) and unanimously approved a 2022 GO bond capital project budget amendment funding Murray-Massenburg, Durham School of the Arts, Glenn Elementary, and other priority projects. The board also unanimously approved the DPS Information Technology hardware refresh and security update plan (including over $4.5 million in ESSER funds and $1.7 million in state/local funds for staff devices and docking stations) and approved the amended February 23 personnel report after closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Celebrations, and Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead opened the meeting, led a moment of silence, and noted that Jovonia Lewis was absent on medical leave. District communications staff recognized Student of the Month Jessica Bortieri (Durham Performance Learning Center), February Teacher of the Month Vade Heddada Rodriguez (Glenn Elementary), and other staff, and announced CROWN Act Week events before Superintendent Pascal Mubenga delivered his update.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review, Approval of Minutes, Public Comment, and Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board amended the agenda to add a capital project amendment and approved the January 26, 2023 monthly meeting minutes. During public comment, speakers urged a resolution against House Bill 187 (reintroducing anti-CRT language from HB 324) and raised safety and injury concerns about deteriorating school track surfaces; the board then unanimously approved the consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: District 3 Vacancy Interview Questions and Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members finalized the District 3 appointment interview format after Board Member Natalie Beyer urged elevating school safety to one of the main prompts alongside superintendent evaluation, equity, and marginalized-community engagement, and letting applicants pick one topic and draw one at random from a bowl for two-minute remarks. With Attorney Malone's guidance, the board agreed to collect conflict-of-interest disclosures in advance and set March 7-8 at 5:30 PM for interviews and March 16 at 5:30 PM for the appointment vote.

agenda_items.title: Capital Project Amendment (2022 GO Bond Kickoff)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Paul LeSieur and Deputy Superintendent Dr. Julius Monk presented a scaled capital project budget amendment initiating 2022 GO bond spending ahead of the county commissioners' February 27 meeting, increasing budgets for Murray-Massenburg ($72 million added for an $83 million total), Glenn Elementary ($59 million total ahead of an April bid), Durham School of the Arts, and staggered priority projects. Board members stressed clarifying for the public that initial DSA amounts do not represent the full construction budget given statewide construction cost escalation.

agenda_items.title: DPS Information Technology Update Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Nakia Hardy and Executive Director of IT Joy Malone presented an overview of DPS IT operations managing nearly 40,000 accounts and 83,000 devices, reduced Fresh Service ticket resolution times, cybersecurity phishing exercises, and a procurement request exceeding $4.5 million in ESSER funds plus over $1.7 million in state/local funds for staff devices and 3,465 docking stations. Board members questioned BrightLink projector replacements, school tech champion stipends, Chromebook damage/loss tracking, and digital literacy around Gaggle monitoring before approving the plan.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Amended Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board entered closed session at 02:21:06 and returned to open session at 03:10:53, where Superintendent Mubenga sought approval of the personnel report as discussed. The board unanimously approved the February 23, 2023 personnel report as amended and adjourned.

votes.discussion_detail: Added the capital project amendment after the District 3 vacancy questions.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved January 26, 2023 board meeting minutes as presented.

votes.item_title: Approval of Capital Project Amendment (2022 GO Bond)

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 2/9/23
meetings.executive_summary: At a nearly seven-hour work session on February 9, 2023—opened with board tributes and a moment of silence after another student death from gun violence impacting Hillside High School—the Durham Public Schools Board of Education accepted Vice Chair Matt Sears's January 31 resignation and experienced a sharp three-round deadlock before electing Emily Chávez as Vice Chair on a 4-2 vote over Jovonia Lewis. The board unanimously approved the District 3 vacancy appointment timeline, a CROWN Act Week resolution, a Leandro funding letter to Governor Roy Cooper, and a CTE Month proclamation, and heard presentations on Equity & Professional Learning and Safety & Security, including the district-wide launch of Gaggle student device monitoring. Later in the evening, the board unanimously approved Superintendent Pascal Mubenga's spending plan for the $18 million MacKenzie Scott donation ($14.5 million net of $3.5 million legally owed to charter schools) after amending it to separate out the $1 million teacher-housing reserve pending an MOU, and also approved the ERP financial/HR system contract subject to board attorney sign-off.

agenda_items.title: Opening Remarks on Hillside High School Tragedy, Agenda Approval, and Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members offered emotional tributes and called for community-wide action on gun violence, mental health counselors, and gun-storage safety following another student death impacting Hillside High School, followed by a moment of silence. The board amended the agenda to add the CROWN Act Week resolution and an Every Child NC Leandro letter, and unanimously approved the January 12, 2023 work session minutes.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public commenters raised concerns over Senate Bill 49 (Parents' Bill of Rights) and student privacy, grieved the Hillside student shooting while urging action on youth safety, and sharply criticized Matt Sears's mid-term resignation to join the DPS Foundation—calling for transparency around board members leaving office for a partner organization receiving district funds.

agenda_items.title: Acceptance of Matt Sears's Resignation and Election of Vice Chair
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously accepted Matt Sears's resignation effective January 31, 2023. Following a coin toss to set voting order after simultaneous nominations of Emily Chávez (by Natalie Beyer) and Jovonia Lewis (by Alexandra Valladares), the board deadlocked 3-3 on Chávez in Round 1 and 3-3 on Lewis in Round 2 amid candid debate over board exclusion, rotational leadership, and experience, before electing Emily Chávez Vice Chair 4-2 on Round 3 when Chair Bettina Umstead switched her vote to break the tie.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Resignation Passed 6-0; Vice Chair: Chávez 3-3, Lewis 3-3, Chávez Elected 4-2

agenda_items.title: District 3 Board Vacancy Appointment Process and Conflict-of-Interest Policy Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members reviewed and approved the application statement of interest and 60-day appointment schedule (due Feb. 27, interviews March 7-8), adding an equity question and preferred pronouns field. Jovonia Lewis asked board counsel whether an MOU or waiting period should govern board members departing for the DPS Foundation to avoid the appearance of conflict of interest, prompting Natalie Beyer to defend Matt Sears's and former member Mike Lee/Casein's ethics while supporting clarity.

agenda_items.title: CROWN Act Week Resolution, Every Child NC Leandro Letter, and CTE Month Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board read and unanimously adopted the CROWN Act Week resolution affirming natural hair and prohibiting race-based hair discrimination, approved sending Every Child NC's Leandro funding letter urging Governor Roy Cooper to protect recurring years 2 and 3 Leandro investments from budget cuts, and adopted Dr. Julie Pack's proclamation declaring February 2023 Career and Technical Education (CTE) Month.

agenda_items.title: Academic Services Updates: Equity & Professional Learning and Safety, Security & Gaggle
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Kelvin Bullock presented updates on the consolidated Office of Equity and Professional Learning, including LETRS literacy training, 12 beginning-teacher mentors, and Policy 1735/1900 training. Safety Director Eva Howard, IT Director Joy Malone, and Dr. Laverne Maddox-Perry then detailed campus security cameras, Zscaler web filtering, 17 Sheriff's Office SROs, and the January 23, 2023 district-wide launch of Gaggle 24/7 monitoring (which reviewed 6,578 items in its first seven days and includes 911 wellness-check protocols when families cannot be reached).

agenda_items.title: MacKenzie Scott $18 Million Donation Spending Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Pascal Mubenga and cabinet leaders presented the $18 million MacKenzie Scott donation allocation—subtracting $3.5 million legally owed to charter schools and dedicating $8.22 million to academics (summer institute PD, Growing Together elementary arts/STEM/world languages, CTE buses/fire truck/ambulance/food truck, $500,000 Family Engagement Center, $280,000 DPS Foundation Whole School Initiative, and $1 million teacher housing reserve), $2.5 million to HR pipelines, $1.5 million to transportation/white fleet EVs, $1.28 million to school support, and $1 million to emergency radios. After Jovonia Lewis objected to placing the $1 million teacher housing reserve with the DPS Foundation without an RFP, the board amended the motion to separate the $1 million housing item pending a future MOU/partner decision.

agenda_items.title: FY 2023-24 Operations Budget Preview and Financial/HR ERP System Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Although board members moved to defer detailed budget discussion due to the late hour, CFO Paul LeSieur briefly reviewed deferred budget items, projected state salary/retirement increases, enrollment loss impacts (24 lost state teaching positions), and board questions on funding the classified salary study versus a potential local parental-leave working group. The board then unanimously approved the new financial and human resources (ERP) system contract subject to board attorney approval.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board entered closed session at 06:14:47 and returned at 06:48:56, unanimously approving the February 9, 2023 personnel report before adjourning.

votes.item_title: Approval of Agenda as Amended
votes.discussion_detail: Added CROWN Act Week resolution (6C) and Every Child NC Leandro letter to Governor Cooper (6D); seconded simultaneously by Millicent Rogers and Jovonia Lewis.

votes.item_title: Approval of January 12, 2023 Work Session Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Approved January 12, 2023 work session minutes as presented.

votes.item_title: Acceptance of Resignation of Board Member Matt Sears
votes.discussion_detail: Accepted Matt Sears's resignation from the District 3 seat effective January 31, 2023 to join the DPS Foundation.

votes.item_title: Election of Board Vice Chair - Round 1 (Nomination of Emily Chávez)
votes.notes: Nominations do not require a second under board policy.
votes.discussion_detail: First voice roll call on Emily Chávez after a coin toss placed her first in voting order; resulted in a 3-3 tie.

votes.item_title: Election of Board Vice Chair - Round 2 (Nomination of Jovonia Lewis)
votes.notes: Chair Bettina Umstead announced the 3-3 tie and proceeded to Round 3.
votes.discussion_detail: Second voice roll call on Jovonia Lewis following speeches by both candidates and Alexandra Valladares; also resulted in a 3-3 tie.

votes.item_title: Election of Board Vice Chair - Round 3 (Nomination of Emily Chávez)
votes.discussion_detail: Bettina Umstead shifted her vote to Aye in the third round to break the 3-3 deadlock and elect Emily Chávez as Vice Chair, noting both nominees were qualified and the board needed to move forward with its agenda.

votes.item_title: Approval of District 3 Vacancy Appointment Process and Timeline
votes.discussion_detail: Approved posting the District 3 statement of interest (with added equity question and pronoun field) due February 27, with interviews on March 7-8, 2023.

votes.item_title: Adoption of CROWN Act Week Resolution
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the CROWN Act Week resolution affirming natural hair and prohibiting race-based hair discrimination in DPS schools.

votes.item_title: Approval of Every Child NC Leandro Letter to Governor Cooper
votes.discussion_detail: Approved sending the Every Child NC letter urging Governor Roy Cooper to protect recurring years 2 and 3 Leandro investments in the state base budget.

votes.item_title: Adoption of Career and Technical Education (CTE) Month Proclamation
votes.discussion_detail: Proclaimed February 1-28, 2023 as Career and Technical Education Month.

votes.item_title: Approval of MacKenzie Scott $18 Million Donation Spending Plan (Separating $1M Teacher Housing Earmark)
votes.discussion_detail: Approved acceptance and allocation of the $18 million MacKenzie Scott donation ($14.5M after $3.5M charter share), amended to separate out the $1 million teacher-housing reserve from the DPS Foundation pending a board-approved MOU and partner review.

votes.item_title: Approval of Financial and Human Resources (ERP) System Contract Subject to Board Attorney Approval
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the contract for the new financial and human resource system subject to final contract language review by the board attorney.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
votes.discussion_detail: Board entered closed session for reasons stated on the agenda.

votes.item_title: Approval of Personnel Report Dated February 9, 2023
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the February 9, 2023 personnel report following closed session.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 2/9/23
disagreements.issue: Election of Board Vice Chair and Board Communication/Leadership Process
disagreements.summary: Following Matt Sears's resignation, the board split 3-3 across two rounds between nominees Emily Chávez and Jovonia Lewis amid pointed debate over rotational leadership, prior experience, and alleged cliques/exclusionary communication before Chair Bettina Umstead broke the tie for Chávez on the third ballot.
disagreements.side_a_position: Elect Emily Chávez as Vice Chair to bring new energy, rotational leadership, and collaborative focus
side_a_arguments: Chávez brought budget advisory co-chair experience, an intersectional equity lens, and strong relationships with commissioners and colleagues.
Supporting Chávez aligned with rotational leadership and moving the board's agenda forward after two deadlocked ballots.
disagreements.side_b_position: Elect Jovonia Lewis based on three years of board experience and push back against perceived pre-arranged cliques and exclusionary communication
side_b_arguments: Lewis argued that after three years on the board—including pandemic leadership and prior service—experience and transparency should outweigh experimentation, noting Beyer had previously said she lacked experience in her first year.
Valladares criticized perceived pre-arranged whip counts, side meetings with partners like the DPS Foundation and Self-Help, and inequitable communication excluding certain board members.
disagreements.resolution: After Round 1 (Chávez) and Round 2 (Lewis) both tied 3-3, Bettina Umstead switched from voting against both nominees to voting Aye for Emily Chávez in Round 3, electing Chávez 4-2; Valladares requested Policy Committee review of Policy 220 officer terms.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 2/9/23
disagreements.issue: Board Member Resignations for DPS Foundation Roles and Conflict-of-Interest Guidelines
disagreements.summary: Following public criticism of Matt Sears resigning to join the DPS Foundation shortly after another former member did the same, board members differed on whether to pursue MOU/policy guardrails on board-to-foundation transitions versus defending former members' ethics.
disagreements.side_a_position: Explore MOU or board policy guidelines (such as recusal during interviews or a cooling-off period) to prevent the appearance of conflicts of interest
side_a_arguments: The public raised concerns about two board members stepping down to work at the DPS Foundation while participating in budget and housing discussions involving the foundation.
Clearer notice or cooling-off rules in an MOU could protect public trust without implying wrongdoing.
disagreements.side_b_position: Defend the ethical record of former members and avoid implying misconduct or adopting overly broad restrictions
side_b_arguments: Board counsel (Tharrington Smith) confirmed no legal conflict existed and both former members stepped down voluntarily to avoid even the appearance of conflict.
Legal counsel cautioned against foundation-specific rules that could hinder employment or complicate partnerships with aligned nonprofits.
disagreements.resolution: No formal motion was taken on an MOU change; later in the meeting, Lewis's request to separate the $1 million teacher-housing reserve from the DPS Foundation in the MacKenzie Scott grant motion was adopted unanimously.
